===PAGE page_0238===
JapaneseFromZero.com 238

The only verb in this lesson that isn't regular is くる (come). Remember: irregular 
verbs don't follow the chart we showed you earlier - their patterns have to be 
memorized.

くる is conjugated as follows:

き ます                                              will come, do come
き ませ ん                                         won't come, don't come
き まし た                                          came
き ませ ん でし た                                didn't come

□ Location particles に and へ
Now that we have verbs to get you moving, where are you going? That's what location 
particles are for.

に and へ (although written as へ, it's pronounced as え) are both location and destination 
particles. They are placed after locations. In English, に and へ can both mean “to.”

There are differences where に and へ are used. に is used when going to an exact 
location, as in, "I am going to France" (Furansu に い ます). The particle へ is used when 
going in a general direction, as in "I am going to the south" (みなみへ い ます).

In modern Japan most Japanese people freely mix に and へ without regard to grammatical 
rules. It would not be wrong to say Furansu へ い ます. The key point to remember is that 
locations require a location marker. In order to prevent confusion, from this point on we will 
use に as the standard location and destination marker.

に as a location marker

Examples
とうきょう に                                        to Tokyo
がっこう に                                          to school
ぎんこう に                                          to the bank
にほん に                                            to Japan

===PAGE page_0239===
Japanese From Zero! – Lesson 12 – Japanese Verbs 239

Now let's combine locations with the verbs.

Example Sentences
1. とうきょう に い ます。                            I am going to Tokyo.
2. ぎんこう に い まし た。                          I went to the bank.
3. がっこう に い ませ ん でし た。                I didn't go to school.
4. おおさか に い ませ ん。                         I am not going to Osaka.

□ Time particle に
に is also used to mark time in a sentence. When used with time it can mean "in", "on", or 
"at".

に as a time marker

Examples
いちがつ に                                          in January
かようび に                                          on Tuesday
ろくじ に                                            at six o'clock

Now let's combine times with the verbs.

Example Sentences
1. いちがつ に い ます。                            I am going in January.
2. かようび に い まし た。                          I went on Tuesday.

□ Time particle usage with きょう、せんしゅう、らいねん etc.
You do not need to add a time particle to words like きょう (today)、あした (tomorrow) etc.
These words are not "specific times" like "Monday" or "January". Adding に after them 
would be as strange as saying "I am going ON tomorrow" or "I didn't go ON yesterday".

This rule is the same for words such as "this week", "next month", "last year", etc.
An easy way to remember this rule is: "If you don't use IN, ON, or AT in English, then don't 
use に in Japanese." Look at the following examples:

Example Sentences
1. らいしゅう い ます。                              I am going next week.
2. きのう い まし た。                              I went yesterday.
3. きょねん い ませ ん でし た。                    I didn't go last year.
4. こんしゅう い ませ ん。                         I am not going this week.

===PAGE page_0240===
JapaneseFromZero.com 240

□ Sentence structure using verbs
Verbs always come last in Japanese sentences. And just like か is added to です to make a 
question, you can add か after the conjugated verb to make a question. In the following 
examples we will use time, location, and question words.

Example Q&A
1. どこ に い ます か。
Where are you going (to)?

にほん に い ます。
I am going to Japan.

2. いえ に かえり まし た か。
Did you return home?

いいえ、ともだちのいえ に い まし た。
No, I went to a friend's house.

3. いつ き ます か。
When are you coming?
さんがつ に い ます。
I will go in March.

4. なん にち に い ます か。
What day of the month are you going?

ふつか に い ます。
I am going on the 2nd.

5. いつ にほん に い ます か。
When are you going to Japan?

らいねんの いちがつ に い ます。
I am going next January.

6. きのう、がっこう に い まし た か。
Did you go to school yesterday?

いいえ、い ませ ん でし た。でも、あした い ます。
No, I didn't go. But I will go tomorrow.

===PAGE page_0241===
Japanese From Zero! – Lesson 12 – Japanese Verbs 241

Using the verb わかる
When using わかる to say that you understand something, you must use が to mark the 
thing that you understand.

Example Sentences
1. にほんご が わかり ます。                       I understand Japanese.
2. にほんご が わかり ませ ん。                    I don't understand Japanese.
3. かれ は えいご が わかり ませ ん。             He doesn't understand English.

Languages and nationalities
By adding ご (language) and じん (people) after a country name, you can create languages 
and nationalities. For example, Spain in Japanese is “supein”. To say “Spanish language,” 
you say supein ご. Russia in Japanese is “roshia”. To say someone is Russian, you say 
roshia じん.

English                 Country                 People                  Language
Japan                   にほん                  にほんじん              にほんご
Korea                   かんこく                かんこくじん            かんこくご
China                   ちゅうごく              ちゅうごくじん          ちゅうごくご
Spain                   supein                  supein じん             supein ご

Note: This works for many countries but not all.

English                 Country                 People                  Language
America                 amerika                 amerika じん            えいご
Philippines             firipin                 firipin じん            tagaragu ご
Mexico                  mekishiko               mekishiko じん          supein ご

Example Sentences
1. Furansu ご が わかり ます か。                   Do you understand French?
2. Jon さん は kanada じん です。                   Jon is Canadian.
3. ようこさん は supein ご が はなせ ます。         Youko can speak Spanish.

12 Q&A しつもん と こたえ E→J

1. When are you coming back?                    いつ かえり ます か。
I will return in May.                          5 がつ に かえり ます。
I will return on the 22nd.                     22 にち に かえり ます。
I will return next week.                       らいしゅう かえり ます。

===PAGE page_0242===
JapaneseFromZero.com 242

2. Are you going?                                   い ます か。
Yes, I am going.                                    はい、い ます。
No, I am not going.                                 いいえ、い ませ ん。

3. Where are you going?                             どこ に い ます か。
I am going to Miyazaki City.                        みやざきし に い ます。
I am going to a friend's house.                     ともだちのいえ に い ます。
I am going to the Hyougo Prefecture.                ひょうごけん に い ます。

4. Are you going to Tokyo?                          とうきょう に い ます か。
Yes, I am going to Tokyo.                           はい、とうきょう に い ます。
No, I am not going to Tokyo.                        いいえ、とうきょう に い ませ ん。

5. Are you coming to the party?                     Pa-ti- に き ます か。
Yes, I am going.                                    はい、い ます。
No, I am not going.                                 いいえ、い ませ ん。

6. Did you go to Japan?                             にほん に い まし た か。
Yes, I went to Japan.                               はい、にほん に い まし た。
No, I didn't go to Japan.                           いいえ、にほん に い ませ ん でし た。

7. When are you coming back?                        いつ かえり ます か。
I will return tomorrow.                             あした かえり ます。
I will return on Sunday.                            にちようび に かえり ます。

8. Will you come (over) tomorrow?                   あした、き ます か。
Yes, I will go.                                     はい、い ます。
No, I won't go.                                     いいえ、い ませ ん。
No, I will go the day after tomorrow.               いいえ、あさって い ます。

9. When did you return to Canada?                   いつ kanada に かえり まし た か。
I didn't return.                                    かえり ませ ん でし た。
I came back on Wednesday.                           すいようび に かえり まし た。

10. What nationality are you?                       なに じん です か。
I am Mexican.                                       Mekishiko じん です。
I am Korean.                                        かんこくじん です。
I am Chinese.                                       ちゅうごくじん です。
I am American.                                      Amerika じん です。
